recommended_phases.title: Phase 1: Domain Primitives — leave-type & leave-status
recommended_phases.rationale: Zero-dependency enums that every other module references. Must exist first.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 2: Employee module
recommended_phases.rationale: Employee model and repository interface — needed by leave-request, leave-balance, notification, and leave. No dependency on other leave modules.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 3: leave-policy module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends only on leave-type. Defines accrual rules, max balances, and approval rules per leave type.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 4: leave-request module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-type, leave-status, and employee. Model + repository interface for the leave request aggregate.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 5: leave-balance module
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on leave-type and employee. Model, repository interface, service interface, and service implementation for balance tracking.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 6: Cross-cutting — audit-log & notification
recommended_phases.rationale: Audit-log has no leave-module deps. Notification depends only on employee. Both are consumed by the leave orchestrator.

recommended_phases.title: Phase 7: leave module (orchestrator)
recommended_phases.rationale: Depends on all modules above. Contains ILeaveService, LeaveService (orchestrates apply/approve/reject/cancel with balance checks, policy validation, audit recording, and notifications), controller, routes, and validation schemas.

app_notes:
## Layer Boundaries

**Domain (innermost):** leave-type, leave-status — pure enums, zero dependencies.

**Domain models + repository interfaces:** employee, leave-policy, leave-request, leave-balance — each owns its model and repository interface. No service logic here.

**Domain services:** leave-balance also owns ILeaveBalanceService + implementation (balance arithmetic is self-contained domain logic).

**Infrastructure:** audit-log (GP-002 compliance), notification — cross-cutting services consumed by the application layer.

**Application (outermost):** leave module — orchestrates the full workflow. Owns ILeaveService, LeaveService, controller, routes, and Fastify validation schemas (GP-003).

## Dependency Flow (all inward)

```
leave (app orchestrator)
 ├── leave-request
 │    ├── leave-type
 │    ├── leave-status
 │    └── employee
 ├── leave-balance
 │    ├── leave-type
 │    └── employee
 ├── leave-policy → leave-type
 ├── audit-log (no leave deps)
 ├── notification → employee
 └── employee
```

No circular dependencies. Every module exposes only its public entry point (index.ts).

## Golden Principles Coverage

- **GP-001 (Repository):** All data access through ILeaveRequestRepository, ILeaveBalanceRepository, ILeavePolicyRepository, IEmployeeRepository, IAuditLogRepository.
- **GP-002 (Audit):** LeaveService calls IAuditLogService.record() on every state change (apply, approve, reject, cancel).
- **GP-003 (Validation):** leaveValidationSchemas in the leave module validate all inputs at the Fastify route boundary.
- **GP-005 (RBAC):** leaveRoutes enforce role checks — employees can apply/cancel own leave; managers can approve/reject team requests.
- **GP-006 (Error):** All async service methods use try/catch; controller wraps in try/catch with proper Fastify error replies.
